title: Cleanroom HVAC Capex Split Across Three Requisitions
scenario_text:
A capital-controls audit agent at Haldane Labs is reviewing authorization on a facilities upgrade project.

**Capital Expenditure Authority Matrix**
- Up to $50,000: Site Director.
- $50,001-$150,000: VP Operations AND Finance review (business case attached).
- Above $150,000: CFO approval AND Audit Committee notification.
- Anti-splitting rule: 'Purchase orders that fund a single project or asset may not be divided to remain under an approval limit. The aggregate value of POs sharing a project code or serving one asset determines the governing tier.'

**Coupa Purchase Orders**
- PO-5510: Vendor 'CleanAir Systems', $48,000, approved by Site Director (Devi N.), 2026-10-05.
- PO-5511: Vendor 'CleanAir Systems', $47,500, approved by Site Director (Devi N.), 2026-10-06.
- PO-5512: Vendor 'CleanAir Systems', $44,500, approved by Site Director (Devi N.), 2026-10-06.
- All three cite project code PRJ-77 and the scope 'Cleanroom C HVAC recirculation upgrade (single commissioned system)'.

**Slack #facilities-capex (reconstructed)**
- Buyer: 'CleanAir bid the Cleanroom C HVAC upgrade at $140,000 total.'
- Devi N. (Site Director): 'Break it into three POs under $50K each so I can approve. One PO and it goes to VP Ops and Finance with the business case.'
- Buyer: 'Cut PO-5510, PO-5511, PO-5512 - all approved by you.'

No VP Operations approval, Finance review, or business case appears in Coupa, Slack, or email. The three POs fund one commissioned HVAC recirculation system for Cleanroom C under a single project code.
question: Applying the anti-splitting rule, what is the governing aggregate value that determines the required approval tier for this project?
